author: reek
body: A literal pattern must match on a unit type exactly as it does on the type inside the wrapper. `emit-pattern-lit-test` dispatches on the scrutinee type, and until 2026-07-28 it dispatched on the WRAPPER: a unit Text missed the TextTy arm and fell to the otherwise arm, which compares the register against `pat-lit-to-integer` of the spelling. The register holds a pointer, so the arm could never match: `when (Name "sin") is "sin"` took the catchall. Measured on seed 759D3E0F and again, identically, on 6ED0A257.

author: reek
body: This one is silent, which is why it is worth a test of its own rather than a line in the show pin. Nothing is printed oddly and nothing faults; the program simply takes a branch it should not have taken. The same hole in `show` at least produced a visibly absurd number.

author: reek
body: Two controls, and the test means nothing without them. `text-plain` is the same match on an unwrapped Text and must match under every reading -- without it, a compiler that had broken literal patterns outright would look identical here. `int-unit` is a literal pattern on a unit Integer, where the otherwise arm is the CORRECT destination, so it must match under every reading too; it is the row that says the fix strips the wrapper rather than sending everything to the Text arm.
